structure:
[part 1] California History-Social Science Framework (2016), a 855-page K-12 framework. Front matter (cover, publishing info, contents, foreword, acknowledgments) then Chapter 1 Introduction and Chapter 2 'Instructional Practice K-Grade Five' (running header 'K-Grade Five' on each page; contains Disciplinary Thinking and Analysis Skills, literacy, ELD, research guidance). Chapters 3-8 are grade chapters (Kindergarten, Grade One ... Grade Five), each opening with a chapter/grade title, bulleted guiding questions (extracted as 'n' bullet units and wrapped lines), an overview, then unit narratives headed by topic subheadings (each keyed to content standards such as K.1, 1.4, 5.6) with guiding questions, plus 'Grade X Classroom Example' boxes (title, ELA/ELD strategy, 'Example (continued)' on following pages, ending in a 'CA HSS Content Standard / CA CCSS / CA ELD' citation line). The formal content standards text is not in this range; it is in Appendix C later in the document. Within this range, grade chapters are narrative description of what students study, so labeled examples with the chapter grade. Running headers give chapter number. Table cells appear only inside classroom examples (ELD table in Ch2; classroom constitution organizer in Ch6; Preamble sentence-deconstruction tables in Ch8). Range ends at u1272 which does not exist in the view; last unit in range is u1271 (Grade Five 'Life in the Young Republic', page 135).
[part 2] California History-Social Science Framework (2016), 855 pp. Part covers Ch 8 end (Grade Five, p.136-139), Ch 9 Instructional Practice Grades 6-8, Ch 10 Grade Six World History and Geography: Ancient Civilizations, Ch 11 Grade Seven Medieval and Early Modern Times, and Ch 12 start (Grade Eight US History, p.250-262). Each grade chapter opens with a title and a bulleted list of guiding questions (extracted with stray 'n'/'nn' bullet glyph fragments), then content narrative organized by unit headings (units with guiding questions followed by narrative); quoted standards text is not reproduced here (formal standards are in Appendix C). Classroom Example boxes begin with a heading 'Grade X Classroom Example: ...', continue after page breaks with 'Example (continued)', and end with a line 'CA HSS Content Standard: ... CA Analysis Skills ... CA CCSS ... CA ELD ...'. Grade is given by the chapter, the running header 'Grade Five/Six/Seven/Eight' (extracted as a unit at the top of every page) and the page-marker running header 'Chapter N'. Chapter 9 is a grades 6-8 instructional-practice chapter (disciplinary skills, literacy, ELD, research) with no content standards.
[part 3] California History-Social Science Framework (2016), K-12, organized by numbered chapters; running page headers 'Grade Eight'/'Grade Nine'/'Grade Ten'/'Grades Nine-Twelve' appear as text units at the top of each page (labeled backup). This part covers the end of Ch12 (Grade 8: units Envisioning a New America, Divergent Paths of the American People 1800-1850, Causes/Course/Consequences of the Civil War, Rise of Industrial America 1877-1914), Ch13 (Instructional Practice for Grades 9-12, backup), Ch14 (Grade 9 elective courses, each introduced by a course-title heading, a guiding question in 'n n' bullet lines, narrative, and Classroom Example boxes), and Ch15 (Grade 10 World History, Culture, and Geography: The Modern World, organized by unit headings with bulleted guiding questions, narrative, and Classroom Example boxes). Classroom Example boxes start with a heading 'Grade X Classroom Example: ...', continue after page breaks with 'Example (continued)', and end with an alignment line 'CA HSS Content Standard(s): ... CA HSS Analysis Skills ... CA CCSS ... CA ELD Standards ...'. No formal standards text (Appendix C) falls in this range; all chapter narrative, guiding questions, vignettes are 'examples'.
[part 4] California History-Social Science Framework (2016), narrative framework, not a standards table. Chapters are grade/course chapters: Ch.15 Grade Ten (continues from earlier part; this range holds its last pages), Ch.16 Grade Eleven (US history, late 19th c. to present), Ch.17 Grade Twelve Principles of American Democracy (one semester), Ch.18 Grade Twelve Principles of Economics (one semester), Ch.19 Assessment (backup). Each page repeats a one-line grade header (e.g. 'Grade Eleven') as a text unit, labeled backup; running headers show 'Chapter N | California History-Social Science Framework'. Chapters open with a title and a stack of guiding questions (bullets rendered as 'n'/'nn'), then course overview narrative, then unit headings (e.g. 'The 1920s', 'Fundamental Principles of American Democracy') each with guiding questions and narrative. 'Grade X Classroom Example: ...' vignette boxes continue across pages with 'Example (continued)' and end with a 'CA HSS Content Standard: ... CA HSS Analysis Skills ... CCSS ... ELD' alignment line; these are labeled examples. Formal standards (codes like 11.2.1, PAD 12.4) are only cited, not reproduced, in this range; they are in Appendix C (outside range). Ch.19 contains figures 19.1-19.5 extracted as table cells (T1 Rn Cn).
[part 5] Part 5 of the 2016 California History-Social Science Framework (book pages ~513-660). Covers the end of Chapter 19 (Assessment of Proficiency in HSS), Chapter 20 (Access and Equity), Chapter 21 (Instructional Strategies), Chapter 22 (Professional Learning), Chapter 23 (Criteria for Evaluating Instructional Materials K-8), Appendix A (Capacities of Literate Individuals) and the start of Appendix B (Problems, Questions, and Themes; Key Theme 1 Patterns of Population). None of these are grade/course chapters or Appendix C standards: they are cross-grade pedagogy, equity, assessment, professional-learning and evaluation-criteria text, so they are backup for all grades. Chapters are marked by 'CHAPTER nn Title' headings and running headers; figures are numbered (Figure 20.1-21.14) and sometimes extracted as table cells [T# R# C#]. Embedded classroom examples (Jamestown grade 5, Civil War grade 8, Grade 11 designated ELD, Moctezuma/Cortes, Cold War grade 11, tenth-grade museum exhibit) are pedagogical vignettes in chapters 19-21 and are labeled backup per the state guide. Appendix B is a general-pedagogy essay on historical problems and themes; the Key Theme 1 narrative (population patterns) is content narrative with sample questions for grades 5-8, 10, 11, labeled examples.
[part 6] Part 6 covers the end of Appendix B 'Problems, Questions, and Themes in the History and Geography Classroom' (book pp. 659-691): the seven Key Themes (narrative essays each ending with a '* * * * *' summary), with running header/footer lines kept as units. Appendix B states the themes and sample questions are for grades five through eight and ten and eleven, so they are labeled examples with those grades. Appendix C (standards) begins right after u6771.
[part 7] California History-Social Science Framework (2016) pages 692-806 of the range: Appendix C reproduces the 1998 History-Social Science Content Standards. Sections: K-5 Historical and Social Sciences Analysis Skills (Chronological and Spatial Thinking; Research, Evidence, and Point of View; Historical Interpretation); then per-grade blocks 'KINDERGARTEN', 'GRADE ONE' ... 'GRADE EIGHT', each with a title/theme, an overview paragraph, and numbered standards 'G.n Students ...' with numbered sub-standards '1.', '2.' beneath (code form grade.standard.item, e.g. 5.3 and item 4 = 5.3.4). 6-8 and 9-12 analysis-skills blocks precede grades 6 and 9-12. Grades 9-12 content: Grade Ten World History, Culture, and Geography: The Modern World (10.1-10.11), Grade Eleven United States History and Geography: Continuity and Change in the Twentieth Century (11.1-11.11), Grade Twelve Principles of American Democracy (12.1-12.10) and Principles of Economics (12.1-12.6). Page header 'History-Social Science Content Standards' and page footers 'California History-Social Science Framework | Appendix C' appear as units. Followed by non-standards appendices: D Teaching the Contemporary World (essay on four themes + suggested readings), E Educating for Democracy (civic education), F Religion and History-Social Science Education (guidelines and legal text), G California Education and the Environment Initiative (Environmental Principles and Concepts; the part of G with grade-by-grade curriculum units lies after u8058). Blank pages 'This page is intentionally left blank.' occur between appendices.
[part 8] Tail of the 855-page HSS Framework (book pp. ~805-855): Appendix G (California Education and the Environment Initiative: EP&C principles, then curriculum units listed under grade headings KINDERGARTEN...ELEVENTH GRADE, TWELFTH GRADE: PRINCIPLES OF AMERICAN DEMOCRACY / ECONOMICS, each with quoted standard codes e.g. 8.6.3 and a CURRICULUM UNIT description), Appendix H (Service-Learning), Works Cited, Framework Resources. No grade 9 in Appendix G. Per state guide, appendices G/H, Works Cited and Resources are backup; Appendix G grade sections are tagged with the grade they name.
